Pass2 Summary: UK Rail Digital Landscape — Current-State Functionality & Passenger-Needs Audit (Pass 2)

As-is public-web baseline checked 2026-09-09. Scope: functionality, content/service architecture, passenger needs, journey coverage, fragmentation, duplication and evidence gaps. This workbook intentionally makes no future GBR recommendations.

Passengers move among a national information layer (National Rail), operator/retailer transaction layers, and shared/supplier platforms for assistance, compensation, parking, lost property, alerts and upgrades.
National Rail is broadest at network information, not transaction ownership
It supports journey/fare comparison, live information, station/accessibility data and guidance, but ticket checkout, refunds and Delay Repay are handed to retailers/operators.

Journey planning, live information, station content, ticket explanations, accessibility and support appear across national, operator and retailer sites; some repetition is necessary, but account/service boundaries remain fragmented.
Refunds, Delay Repay, complaints and lost property commonly move from a branded operator site to a separate portal or supplier, sometimes with a different account.
Smartcards and PAYG exist across Key/KeyGo, Tap2Go, c2c Smartcard/TfL, GWR Touch, MetroSmart, ScotRail and other schemes rather than one common passenger account.
Differentiation clusters around operator-specific service propositions
Examples include loyalty/rewards, automated compensation, seat choice, crowding information, virtual station tours, specialist accessibility guides, upgrade auctions and onboard services.
Accessibility is both national and distributed

National Rail provides station/accessibility data and Passenger Assistance provides a reusable assistance profile/request service, while TOCs repeat local accessibility, meeting-point and travel-support information.
International rail has its own fragmented acquisition layer
BritRail information, international sales agents, Eurostar and specialist reservation processes create separate paths from domestic National Rail retail.
Public-web research cannot expose all system boundaries
Identity sharing, supplier ownership, authenticated account functions, app-only features, data lineage and live-data coverage require SME validation before strategic decisions.

✓ in the comparison matrix means confirmed from the checked public web estate. — means the capability was not found after checking the current public estate or is explicitly handed off elsewhere; it does not claim that no internal capability exists. ? means evidence was insufficient. Capabilities behind authentication, mobile-app-only functions, supplier ownership, data lineage and uncertain legacy services are explicitly routed to the SME Validation sheet. The audit distinguishes necessary distributed information from genuine duplication/fragmentation and records operator-specific capabilities without treating them as universal passenger requirements.
